findings.claim: In checkIfIsAvailable, the new workingHours branch sets both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. That means `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that extends past the end of the working window, so availability can be granted for slots that overlap the boundary.
findings.title: Working-hours check compares the slot start minute to itself, so it never rejects slots that end after working hours

findings.claim: The new date-override logic checks `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. Since these are distinct Dayjs objects, the equality is always false even when the timestamps are equal. As a result, an override whose start and end are the same instant will not be recognized as an exact match and can be rejected by the surrounding branch logic.
findings.title: Date-override comparison uses object identity instead of value equality, causing exact override matches to be treated as outside the override
